thread:
maria-cs: starting thread — Opal reserved pool smokecheck today 1400 PT. goal: validate quota, autoscale, and rate caps before tomorrow's cutover. can ops + ml join?
chris-ops: I can join. planning to run a ~5m shadow load then a sustained soak. do we have the load profile?
devon-ml: i created a tiny profile based on opal's expected qps. it's conservative: 250 rps peak, avg 120. putting it in the runbook.
sara-reliability: FYI, last reserved run we saw 429 spikes around 200rps due to rate_cap policy on the routing tier. we should check route-level quotas.
maria-cs: noted. @chris-ops can you confirm the quota buckets for Opal org? also request an enablement call with their infra lead after smokecheck.
chris-ops: quota buckets: reserved_pool=opal-resv, per_route=1000req/min default, token_rate=unified. i'll bump per_route to 1800req/min for the test.
chris-ops: test plan snippet: ```k6 run --vus 200 --duration 10m scripts/opal_smoke.js --out influxdb``` will simulate steady 140 rps with spikes to 260 rps for 30s every 2m.
devon-ml: autoscale config I'll apply to the pool (staging): ```autoscale:
  min_replicas: 2
  max_replicas: 18
  cpu_target: 65
  latency_slo_ms: 200
  scale_window: 45s```
sara-reliability: looks good. when spinning up replicas, keep a 2-min cooldown to avoid thrash. set `burst_buffer: 300` to absorb short spikes.
maria-cs: ops, ml — can we add a soft fallback policy to route for 10% of traffic to a smaller model if latency > 350ms? Opal requested graceful degradation to avoid errors.
devon-ml: yes. adding fallback to `redwood-compact-v1` at 10% can buy headroom. will include canary flags.
chris-ops: running the initial shadow run now. watching token-level cost and per-route 429s. deploy-bot: deploy status — reserved pool staging applied (pool-id: rp-opal-17), autoscale policy active.
deploy-bot: canary rollout to fallback enabled for route /v1/generate (10% traffic)
chris-ops: first 3 minutes: 250rps spike triggered new replicas, but got 429s from routing tier at 2:03. looks like rate_cap enforcement happened before pool capacity scaled.
sara-reliability: bumping route per_route to 2400req/min now, adding grace window to rate_cap (60s).
maria-cs: Opal's PM on the call — they saw a couple of request failures in their logs. i informed them it's transient and we're tuning. they asked about renewal impact if we can't hit SLA tomorrow.
devon-ml: we can mitigate by increasing burst_buffer to 600 and temporarily raising max_replicas to 22 for the next 2 hours. want to try that.
chris-ops: done: burst_buffer=600, max_replicas=22. re-running spike test.
chris-ops: spinner: second run shows no 429s, 95th latency ~210ms, median 120ms. no errors in 10m run.
maria-cs: great. i'll schedule the enablement with Opal infra for 1600 PT and surface the tuning notes + cost delta.
sara-reliability: note for postmortem: add a pre-warm step to scale pool 1.5x before known spikes; add ordering: route quota bump before load test to avoid early 429s.
chris-ops: saved load logs to runs/1781234560/opal_smoke_2.csv and linked in runbook.
maria-cs: next steps: 1) deliver enablement deck, 2) get Opal approval to keep temporary settings for 24h, 3) follow up on renewal risk comms if metrics stay green.
devon-ml: I'll open a follow-up PR for the fallback model telemetry so we can track quality delta when fallback triggers.
maria-cs: thanks everyone. :thumbsup: we'll reconvene at 1600 PT after enablement.
